title: the_parkour_run_he_paid_for
display_title: My best friend paid a stranger $200 to beat my parkour record — and I found the receipt
share_line: Send this to the friend who turns your hobby into a competition.
beats: My best friend (26M) paid a random Minecraft server player two hundred dollars to beat my parkour time.
I'd held that record for eight months. It was the one thing on that server that was mine.
He swore he had nothing to do with it, sat right next to me while I rage-quit.
Three weeks later I'm cleaning his Venmo history for a shared game key, and there it is. Two hundred dollars, memo: "for the run lol."
I didn't confront him. I just added him back to my blacklist and let him wonder why.
He still texts asking if I want to run parkour again sometime. So, was I wrong to just go silent instead of telling him I know?
